messages:
acme-customer: We're starting to get intermittent 401 Unauthorized from api.redwood.ai. Happens ~2-3% of requests. Response has no body and no x-request-id header that we can see. Anyone seen this pattern? 
maya_support: Sorry for the trouble — quick q: are you using a long-lived server key or a short-lived session token? Also which SDK + version? 
acme-customer: Server-side key (proj_ scope), node 18, using redwood-node v1.4. Key rotated last week but we updated env. No 401s in logs before today. 
ryan_eng: A couple of places to check for request IDs. 1) If you're calling via curl or SDK, look for response headers `x-request-id` or `x-redwood-request-id`. 2) In Console -> Requests, filter by the API key prefix or client ip/time window and click the row to copy the debug token. That debug token looks like `dbg-<hex>` and is the fastest way for us to find the trace. 
maya_support: To get richer logs from Node SDK set DEBUG=redwood:* or set { debug: true } in client config. The SDK will print the response headers on error. Search your server logs for `x-request-id` or `redwood_request_id`. 
acme-customer: We tried DEBUG and didn't see any header lines when the 401 came back. Also our reverse proxy strips unknown headers — could that remove x-request-id? 
ryan_eng: Yes — if you have a proxy (nginx/HAProxy/Cloud CDN) in front of your service that reissues the request to Redwood, it won't change Redwood's response headers, but if the proxy strips response headers before returning to your app, you won't see them. Try curling from the same host that directly calls Redwood (bypass proxy) or check proxy config for `proxy_hide_header` rules. 
maya_support: If you can run curl directly from your server: 

``
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"test"}' -v
```

Look for `x-request-id` in the response. If it's missing, paste the full response headers here (redact auth). If you get a 401, include the exact response headers and the timestamp (UTC). 
acme-customer: Ran curl from origin host (bypassing proxy), got 401 and this header in server's raw response: `x-request-id: 02A4d6e9f1`. Console debug token for same approx time: `dbg-cf12b9`. Timestamps UTC: 2026-03-20T10:21:11Z and 2026-03-20T10:21:13Z. 
infra_oncall: oncall here — thanks for the token and ids. Two quick checks: (1) confirm the API key prefix you used (proj_ vs svc_); (2) confirm the account/org. If key scope mismatches we can see auth failures on our side and link to request ids. We'll search with dbg-cf12b9 and 02A4d6e9f1. 
maya_support: Also helpful: paste the exact Authorization header value prefix (e.g., `Bearer proj_abc...`) — redact after first 6 chars if posting publicly. If you'd rather not paste keys, DM and we'll create a private escalation. 
acme-customer: Posting a redacted prefix: `Bearer proj_abcdef...`. Sending DM with full curl + raw headers + request id copies. 
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0945. Assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2. 
maya_support: Thanks — once infra correlates the debug token to a serving host and auth service logs we'll update. If we need a HAR (browser) or SDK trace we'll ask — HAR is only for browser flows. For mobile or server SDKs we prefer the raw curl + debug token. 
acme-customer: Understood, appreciate it.
